title: Deferred features are rejected with generic or wrong diagnostics, not structured unsupported diagnostics
Half of test/fixtures reject markers use diagnostic codes that spec/README.md does not define
Sized numeric types (i8-i64, u8-u64, f32) are unimplemented and not listed as deferred
The parser rejects core chapter-02 forms that the reference parser accepts
Prelude names `Any`, `Eq`, `Hash`, and `Hasher` are unknown
Non-public functions may omit their result type (inferred); public ones need missing-result-type
`type` declarations and local type/impl declarations are rejected as syntax errors
Non-public functions may omit their requirement clause (row inferred, least row for cycles)
Exponent must be an unsigned integer type
Reject cases pass even when unrelated errors are also reported
Row-kinded generic data arguments such as `Job[$()]` fail to parse
`is` rejects operands whose static type is `mut T`
`string.replace` is not implemented
A comma at depth zero does not end a same-line suite
Initialization check follows trait dispatch through generic bounds and trait values
A plain `fn` closure may mutate a captured mutable list; the program is accepted and runs
`mut fn` closures are unsupported, and assigning a captured `let` reports `unknown-name`
Mixed-permission list literal reports `no-common-type` instead of `no-least-common-type`
The `disposed-file` runtime profile named in spec/conformance/README.md does not exist
`hd check` does not check `Ok`/`Err` payloads against the expected Result type
`_ := f()?` on `Result[void, E]` emits WAT that Binaryen cannot parse
`hd run` and `hd test` crash with a stack trace when there is no entry point
A `main` returning `Result[void, E]` passes check but cannot run
hd rejects same-line `if c: a else: b`, a form chapter 01 uses as an example
Primitives do not satisfy `T: Display` and cannot become `Display` trait values
`mut fn` closure literals do not parse
`string.trim()` removes U+FEFF and keeps U+0085
A default that names a later parameter reports a code outside the spec inventory
Optional `?` inside a closure emits WAT that Binaryen cannot parse
A generic function cannot be used as a value, even when its type arguments are known
`pub` on a path-only `use` is accepted
`pub` on a top-level binding is accepted
Declared variance is deferred, so covariant data cannot be written
A backslash before a quote in a raw string is a lexer error
Reference-bounded method generics are allowed in dynamic traits
Assigning a tuple element is invalid-assignment-target
Only a pub main is an entry point
Inferred mutable upgrade reports mutable-upgrade
`is` ignores permissions on its operands
Fieldless data values are canonical under `is`
supertrait-cycle is reported once per cycle
